body:
## Hold

Keep this issue blocked until the maintainer reviews #2557 and accepts a measured benefit.
The maintainer deferred implementation until after #2556.
No cloud server is purchased or created under this proposal alone.

## Work

Define a pinned Linux x86-64 image with nextest and compatible runtime libraries.
Include Mesa and xvfb for any later UI execution.
Keep the toolchain on the build runner unless a selected test requires Cargo.
Check CPU instruction support and library compatibility.
Start with two workers and an explicit spending limit.
Keep cloud credentials, GitHub credentials, signing keys, and cache credentials on the trusted controller.
Transfer only the public source, fixtures, compiled tests, and expected manifest to workers.
Use a clean account and an allow-list of environment variables.
Collect results before deletion.
Delete workers after success, failure, cancellation, and timeout.
Use an independent expiry check after controller failure.
Confirm deletion and remove temporary volumes and addresses.
Record resource IDs and costs in the run report.

Keep the existing cut.yml checks for the merge parent and identical trees.
Publish cut-tip.txt only after the complete verdict passes.
Keep the manual cut trigger and the current release permissions.
Update the gate and runners skills when the workflow changes.
Follow the process-change rules for the implementation PR.

Evidence: .github/workflows/cut.yml, xtask/src/checkout.rs, and .claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md.
Public reference: https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/billing/faq/.
Powered-off servers still incur charges.
Use a current quote; the rate in #2557 is historical.

Done means: lifecycle checks cover success, failure, cancellation, timeout, and controller failure.
No temporary worker remains after cleanup.
Workers receive no service credentials.
A failed or incomplete result cannot publish the cut-tip artifact or bypass the tag checks.
The run report includes the approved spending limit and actual resource costs.

Part of #2557
